7. Defendant Nos. 12-13 that Sheikh Selim and Rashid Miah had title and possession ill the suit land described in schedule-II to the plaint two equal shares and accordingly, the, share of Rashid Miah was rightly recorded in his name in the SA Khatian and While possessing the same, he died leaving behind defendant Nos.12-14 as his heirs and defendant Nos.12 and 13 have been possessing the same. For grabbing the land of these defendants, the plaintiff created false girding the Suit land documents regarding the Suit land. 

 16. The respondents claimed that Sam Miah by a registered deed of sale transferred one powa of land out of the 1st scheduled land to his brother, Charu Miah @ Abdul Khalique and handed over the possession to him. Thereafter, Saru Miah gifted .005 acre of land out the 1st scheduled land to Tunu Miah, son of his other brother named Kantu Miah by a registered deed of gift dated 08.12.1979 and during the field survey in the last settlement operation, the 1st scheduled land was recorded in the names of the plaintiff and his said brother according to their respective share and possession in two different khatiang and thus, the plaintiffs had been under the wrong impression that the record of rights of the land prepared naturally and legally during the field survey would be duly published. However, at same time, during the first part of baishakh, 1386 B.S., the plaintiffs upon enquiry were utterly surprised to know that the record of rights of the land described in schedule-II to the plaint which is a part And parcel of the 1st scheduled land belonged to the plaintiff in its totality, had been changed and wrongly recorded in the names of late Kantu Miah and Rashid Miah without any basis and knowledge of the plaintiff and done in the back of the plaintiff. Said Kantu Miah and Rashid Miah, brother-in-law of Sheikh Selim were close relatives of the plaintiff. Having no place to live in, said Kantu Miah and Rashid Miah sought for temporary shelter from the plaintiff during the time of local survey of the last settlement operation and the plaintiffs out of grace permitted them to reside in the land described in schedule-III to the plaint which is a part of the 2nd scheduled land purely for the time being on temporary basis on condition to move away therefrom after arrangement of their own accommodation elsewhere and while they were residing there on permission, said Kantu Miah and Rashid Miah died leaving benind defendant Nos.1-11 and 12-14 as their legal hers respectively. Since defendant Nos.1-14 were very helpless, the plaintiff merely allowed them to reside in the 3"' scheduled land on condition to vacate the same as soon as they would be able to arrange accommodation elsewhere. Defendant No.2 purchased .01 acre of land out of the 2nd scheduled land on the western side of the land of the 3rd scheduled land. The plaintiff having learnt about the wrong and illegal record of rights of the 2nd scheduled land in the names of Kantu Miah and Rashid Miah demanded to defendant Nos.1-14 for correction of the same record of rights and asked them to vacate the land concerned and remove the structures therefrom. Though they initially agreed to take appropriate step for correction of the record, they refused to take any step later and defendant Nos.1 and 2 additionally refused to vacate the 3rd scheduled land when pressed by the plaintiff for the last time by the last part of baishakh, 1386 B.S. Kantu Miah and Rashid Miah had no title or interest of any kind in any of the lands of the suit property and as such, they recorded the land in their names by influencing the survey officials. The wrong and illegal record of rights in respect of the 2nd scheduled land cast cloud over the title of the plaintiff.
